name: Umhausen
kurzbeschreibung: Highest-lying municipality in the vorderen Ötztal, featuring the Stuibenfall, the Ötzi-Dorf, and the natural swimming pond.
beschreibung:
Overview

Umhausen is situated at an elevation of 1,031 meters in the central Ötztal Valley, resting on the expansive alluvial fan of the Horlachbach stream at the foot of Mount Tauferberg. Home to around 3,400 inhabitants, this multifaceted municipality includes the main village, the hamlets of Tumpen, Köfels, Farst, and Östen, as well as the sunny high plateau of Niederthai at 1,550 meters. Recognized as the oldest verified permanent settlement in the Ötztal, Umhausen delights nature enthusiasts and families with an extraordinary wealth of alpine attractions: alongside Tyrol's highest waterfall, the roaring Stuibenfall, the community hosts an open-air archaeological park dedicated to the Stone Age, a bird of prey sanctuary, a pristine bathing lake, and extensive trails on the Niederthai plateau.

History

The topography of Umhausen was sculpted 8,000 to 9,000 years ago by a monumental geological catastrophe: the Köfels rockslide hurled immense stone masses into the valley, damming the stream into a vast lake. When the waters finally carved through the rock barrier, the Stuibenfall waterfall was born. Archaeological discoveries trace continuous habitation back to the Neolithic era. Umhausen was first documented in writing around 1220 AD as the original mother parish of the Ötztal, acting as the historic focal point for the valley's settlement. For centuries, the community was renowned across the region for superior flax cultivation and linen weaving ('Ötztaler Flachs'). In the village center stands the Parish Church of Saint Vitus: recorded in 1220 and enlarged in Late Gothic style in 1482, it has preserved its authentic Gothic architecture with rare 14th-century frescoes.

Getting There

By car, Umhausen is reached via the Inntal Autobahn A12 by taking the Ötztal exit and following the B186 highway south for roughly 18 kilometers directly into the village. An asphalt mountain road winds up seven kilometers to Niederthai. Train passengers arrive at Ötztal-Bahnhof station along the Arlberg Railway. From there, frequent VVT regional bus line 320 runs every 30 minutes to Umhausen, with connecting shuttle buses continuing to Niederthai.

Tips

The crowning natural wonder is the Stuibenfall: plunging 159 meters, it is Tyrol's highest waterfall, accessible via an exhilarating 700-step suspension bridge walkway, panoramic viewing platforms, and a family-friendly via ferrata through the ionized mist. Near the base of the falls, the Ötzi Village (Ötzi-Dorf) reconstructs Neolithic life across a 9,000-square-meter open-air archaeological park, flanked by the Birds of Prey Park Umhausen featuring daily falconry flight demonstrations. On warm summer days, the Umhausen natural bathing lake offers refreshing spring water. In winter, the sun-kissed Niederthai plateau (1,550 meters) transforms into a snow-sure cross-country skiing and winter walking paradise.
